title: Reserve vs Burst capacity plan (queuing & burst cost analysis)
summary: Working spreadsheet-style analysis that compares reserved (preprovisioned) capacity vs burst (on-demand/spot) for production inference. Focus is on how queueing delay, warm-up penalty, and burst hourly rate shape monthly unit economics and SLO attainment across three traffic profiles: steady, diurnal, and spiky (flash sales).
purpose: Provide a pragmatic reserve/burst mix heuristic and a simple model that teams can plug into Redwood Optimize to generate recommendations per-customer or per-route. Emphasis on capturing queueing-induced latency cost and the cost of prewarming GPU instances for sudden demand spikes.
assumptions:
- GPU instance types: g4x-large (baseline), a100-40g (high perf).
- Reserved capacity billed hourly at committed discount (example rates used in sheet).
- Burst capacity billed at on-demand hourly + spot fallback delta.
- Prewarm time: 90s cold-start to steady throughput for g4x-large; warm pre-provision reduces to 10s.
- Queuing model: M/M/c approximation for bursts; median request length in tokens mapped to avg inference time per token.
- Traffic profiles defined by 15-minute bins from historical ingestion data.
- SLO: p95 latency <= 350ms for interactive routes; batch routes tolerate higher latency.
- Model batching scales throughput linearly up to per-GPU concurrency limit.
model_overview: The sheet computes per-bin required GPUs (concurrent workers) to achieve target p95 latency under given batching strategy, then splits GPUs into reserved and burst share. For each bin: compute required_workers = ceil(observed_qps * avg_latency_per_inference / effective_concurrency). Multiply by bin_duration to get reserved_hours and burst_hours. Apply hourly rates. Add prewarm_cost when burst worker count increases beyond recent baseline within 5-minute window.
formulas:
- required_workers = ceil((observed_qps * avg_inference_s) / effective_concurrency)
- reserved_hours = reserved_allocated * bin_hours
- burst_hours = max(0, (required_workers - reserved_allocated)) * bin_hours
- prewarm_cost_monthly = prewarm_count * prewarm_unit_cost * estimated_prewarms_per_month
- monthly_cost = sum(reserved_hours * reserved_rate + burst_hours * burst_rate) + sum(prewarm_cost_monthly)
- cost_per_successful_request = monthly_cost / monthly_successful_requests
- queueing_delay_est = max(0, SLO_target - service_time); tie into penalty if p95 exceeds SLO
recommendations:
1) Baseline reserved allocation = 60th percentile of 15-minute required_workers across last 30 days for interactive routes.
2) For routes with high spike kurtosis (top 15% by kurtosis), maintain a 'buffer bucket' of cheap spot instances pre-warmed to reduce prewarm penalty; budget ~5-8% of monthly cost for spot prewarm to cut tail latency.
3) Use per-route holdback: allocate reserved capacity strictly to top N routes by revenue per token; less-critical routes remain fully burstable.
4) Autoscale thresholds: add burst when bin required_workers > reserved_allocated AND sustained for 2 consecutive 15m bins to avoid churn.
5) Penalize prewarm-heavy strategies when p95 SLO is loose (>=1s); shift to more burst-only if cost savings outweigh occasional latency spikes.
estimated_savings: Sample scenario (mid-size product): moving from 90% reserved to 60% reserved with 5% prewarm buffer reduced monthly spend by ~22% while p95 increased by +40ms; larger customers with smoother diurnal patterns saved up to 34%. Results highly sensitive to spike frequency and prewarm cost assumptions.
sensitivity_analysis: Varying prewarm_unit_cost from $10 to $80 per event -> monthly cost swings by +/- 12% in spike-heavy workloads
If reserved_rate increases by 15% (vendor price change), optimal reserved mix shifts down by ~9 percentage points on average
Reducing warm_preparation_time from 90s to 30s is worth ~3-7% monthly savings because it reduces required prewarm_count
next_steps: 1) Validate with per-customer traffic slices for 10 largest Dedicated customers. 2) Hook this sheet to sandboxed telemetry pipeline to compute real per-bin prewarm_count estimates. 3) Build a small Redwood Optimize rule that surfaces recommended reserved % and expected savings per-route. 4) Sync with infra team on spot/prewarm orchestration feasibility (OPT-233).
notes:
- This is intentionally conservative: we assume linear batching and ignore nonlinear saturation on some models.
- Metrics needed: per-bin GPU utilization, cold-start durations by instance family, per-route revenue per token.
- Cross-check against running 'scale-sim' experiments in github:repo/inference-sim to ensure queueing model matches empirical latencies.
